title: Comparison Between Surcharge And Cess
definition: A surcharge is an additional tax levied on the existing tax liability (income or corporate tax) of individuals and corporations, while a cess is a special-purpose tax levied on top of basic tax rates to fund specific government welfare schemes.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC CSE Prelims (Constitutional provisions, Article 270, divisible pool of taxes, Finance Commission mandates) and Mains GS Paper III (Fiscal federalism, tax buoyancy, resource mobilization, and center-state fiscal relations).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational constitutional provisions governing surcharges and cesses under Articles 269, 270, and 271.
Evaluate the fiscal federalism implications of rising cesses and surcharges on the divisible pool of tax revenues.
Apply high-yield mnemonics and comparative matrices to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basics of Indian Taxation System (Direct and Indirect Taxes)
Constitutional provisions regarding Centre-State financial relations
Role of the Finance Commission of India
